name: End-to-End Lossy Image Compression Benchmark
description: Image compression is one of the most fundamental techniques and commonly used applications in the image and video processing field. Earlier methods built a well-designed pipeline, and efforts were made to improve all modules of the pipeline by handcrafted tuning. Later, tremendous contributions were made, especially when data-driven methods revitalized the domain with their excellent modeling capacities and flexibility in incorporating newly designed modules and constraints. Despite great progress, a systematic benchmark and comprehensive analysis of end-to-end learned image compression methods are lacking. In this paper, we first conduct a comprehensive literature survey of learned image compression methods. The literature is organized based on several aspects to jointly optimize the rate-distortion performance with a neural network, i.e., network architecture, entropy model and rate control. reputation: A well-cited benchmark/survey-style reference in learned image compression that helped consolidate evaluation of end-to-end neural compression methods.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark; results depend on bitrate and distortion metric, so scores are not directly comparable across papers without matching operating points.
